University of Sydney The Bessie Cook Piano Award 2022 is an initiative by the University of Sydney, Australia for outstanding students studying piano at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music. The selected students will receive benefits as determined by the Dean of the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

Established in 2007 from the estate of the late Bessie Catherine Cook, the Bessie Cook Piano Award provides financial assistance to outstanding students to undertake studies in piano at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.
To be eligible, an applicant must -
Be enrolled or have an unconditional offer to study full-time in a coursework or research degree at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music
The selected candidates will receive benefits as determined by the Dean of the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

The scholarship will be awarded on the basis of:
For a postgraduate research applicant, the scholarship will also be awarded on the basis of research achievements and potential.
The applicants will be required to attend an interview.
The scholarship value will be stipulated in the Scholarship Offer Letter to the successful recipient(s).
For a coursework student, the annual payment will be made in two equal instalments after the census date of each semester.
For a postgraduate research student, the value of the scholarship will be paid as a stipend on a fortnightly basis.
Deferral of the scholarship is not permitted.
Suspension of the scholarship may be approved with the written approval of the Dean of the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.
Transfer of the scholarship, within the same faculty, may be permitted with the written approval of the Dean.
The scholarship will be offered subject to the availability of funds.
To continue receipt of the scholarship, the recipient must maintain a minimum Semester Average Mark (SAM) of 65 each semester.
Recipients undertaking an exchange during the tenure of this scholarship are required to have achieved a Satisfied Requirements grade (SR) to receive their next payment.
The scholarship will be terminated if the recipient -
withdraws from an eligible course or fails to enrol
commences part-time study without prior approval of the Dean of the Sydney Conservatorium of Music
does not maintain satisfactory academic performance
is determined by the University to be guilty of serious misconduct, including, but not limited to, having provided false or misleading information as part of their Scholarship application
does not resume study at the end of a period of approved leave.
Once a scholarship has been terminated, it cannot be reinstated.

If a student is found guilty of serious misconduct or the Scholarship is terminated under any instance in the Termination Clause of these terms and conditions, the University reserves the right to request that any scholarship funds paid to the scholarship recipient be reimbursed.
